scope.owned_layer: Supervisor cadence, slow-I/O lock boundaries, bounded cycle telemetry, and lease-bound dispatch-status batching.
scope.not_changing: Dispatch eligibility, dependency or priority policy, worker limits, provider account/quota grouping, reviewer policy, live runtime, deployment, or product services.

findings.finding: A durable launch_intent with no receipt and either no marker or multiple markers was retained forever, so an adapter exception before launch could permanently freeze process_queue and suppress normal quota/auth fallback or reassignment.
findings.resolution: Apply a finite 30-second launch grace capped at 300 seconds, then combine post-intent markers with exact live worker-runner evidence from ORCH_TASK_ID, ORCH_AGENT_ID/ORCH_PROVIDER, ORCH_RUN_ID, PID, and Linux PID start ticks. One live generation is adopted; a conclusive zero-process scan clears an unchanged stale token and retries in the same entry; multiple live generations remain fail-closed.

findings.finding: claim_next_task_for_agent wrapped provider report loading, process_queue worktree/adapter launch, and dashboard rendering in one exclusive runtime-admission transaction.
findings.resolution: Prefetch immutable provider, activity, and planning inputs before admission; execute self-claim against a detached snapshot between a short per-agent reservation and whole-state CAS; render dashboard artifacts only after the CAS. The actual public entry point now proves all three named slow calls execute at lock depth zero.

findings.finding: _run_with_deferred_dispatch_status_syncs flushed canonical dispatch status, archive actions, and activity events after its operation raised even though no successful runtime mutation was proven.
findings.resolution: On operation failure, discard every uncommitted deferred canonical/archive/activity effect and run only exact PID-start-bound termination confirmation before re-raising the original error.

findings.finding: Launch recovery accepted an older same-task/agent worker_runner because the /proc scan never compared its generation with prepared_epoch_seconds, while a 2020 marker could pass the unique-marker fallback after heartbeat rewrites refreshed its mtime and be bound to the new queue_event_id.
findings.resolution: Persist a pre-spawn Linux boot-relative tick boundary, reconstruct every candidate process start epoch from procfs btime plus PID start ticks divided by CLK_TCK, and reject definitively pre-intent generations. Filter runner markers by their immutable started_at at marker timestamp resolution instead of file mtime, so the unique-marker fallback cannot bypass the temporal proof. Keep task, run, and normalized agent/provider identity checks so Codex and Codex2 remain distinct groups.

cadence_reproduction.source: The governed task packet records live 2026-08-02 cycles of approximately 51 to 80 seconds; the referenced live log is intentionally not copied into this source worktree.
cadence_reproduction.overrun_contract: Advance arithmetically to the first future anchored monotonic deadline; skipped starts are counted and never replayed in a zero-sleep loop.

global_lock_order.rule: Slow preparation happens before this order. Lease validation takes runtime admission shared, canonical CAS takes task state exclusive, and the durable activity outbox appends only after the canonical state snapshot is durable.

before_runtime_admission: GitHub bus and merged-PR metadata reads

reserved_runtime_phases.contract: Each phase publishes a token in one short exclusive transaction, performs marker/process/worktree/git/prune I/O against a detached snapshot with audit/status effects deferred, and commits through a second short whole-state CAS. Before adapter delivery, the exact token receives a durable launch intent with wall epoch and boot-relative tick boundary; after successful delivery it receives a complete worker receipt. Recovery combines immutable marker started_at with exact task/agent/run/PID-start process evidence and a procfs btime plus CLK_TCK temporal comparison: one post-intent live generation is adopted, pre-intent generations are excluded before unique-marker fallback, a stale conclusive zero-process intent is cleared, and multiple live generations remain fail-closed. A concurrent writer wins; a losing phase cannot overwrite it, and any newly launched exact process generation is terminated fail-closed.

slow_io_boundaries.fail_closed_git_fallback: A worker base ref missing from the prefetch context may use an already-resolving local ref, but dispatch never starts a recovery network fetch while runtime admission is held; an unresolved ref waits for the next pre-admission fetch.

properties: Exact owner and expected-status CAS is checked for every row before the single durable commit.
Every row revalidates its exact actor, task, run, workspace, and process-generation lease against the shared runtime snapshot.
A late invalid row aborts without calling the canonical commit.
A crash after canonical save leaves one digest-bound activity outbox that recovery appends exactly once.
The outer supervisor process cannot impersonate a worker because each row installs and clears its own status-command binding.

telemetry.persistence: The complete sample is persisted after reserved process/poll/prune phases, deferred activity/status/archive work, dashboard refresh, and runtime summary. The cycle elapsed value therefore covers the whole cycle rather than the former pre-release prefix.
telemetry.lock_hold_contract: Every measured runtime transaction starts its hold timer only after blocking acquisition succeeds and stops it before release; acquisition contention is not reported as exclusive ownership.
telemetry.scheduler_resilience: A cadence completion telemetry exception is isolated and cannot terminate the deadline scheduler or prevent future cycles.
telemetry.privacy: Only aggregate scalar counts and durations are retained; no task payload, provider output, credentials, or unbounded history is stored.

governance_preservation.dispatch_decisions: Existing dependency, priority, worker-limit, failure-loop, chair-review, quota/auth fallback, active-lease, and rollback paths remain unchanged.
governance_preservation.identity: Codex and Codex2 remain distinct configured identities and quota groups; no equivalence or global mutual-review prohibition is introduced.
governance_preservation.review: Human/Ops remains the explicit independent reviewer and must bind its decision to the exact PR head before closeout.

delivery.rollout: Merge the exact Human/Ops-reviewed PR to dev; the dependent V8 canary owns any live promotion.
delivery.rollback: Revert the merge commit; do not hand-edit runtime, canonical task, or activity state.
delivery.remaining: Push the repaired PR head, obtain a new exact-head Human/Ops review, merge, then perform governed done/archive closeout.
